name: Fujicolor PRO 400H Professional
notes: Fujicolor PRO 400H Professional (AF3-176E), Fujifilm Product Information Bulletin, plots on page 8 (nos. 18, 19 and 21); the drawings are vector paths, traced end to end. Date taken from the print code EIGI-05.1-FG(HB) next to the reference number in the footer (read as January 2005; no other date printed). Process printed on the plots: C-41 (the bulletin says: Process C-41 or equivalent, as well as Fujifilm CN-16).

Speed: daylight and electronic flash ISO 400/27 degrees; 3200 K tungsten ISO 100/21 degrees with Wratten 80A (or LBB-12). No Log H Ref is printed (log_h_ref null); no printing paper is named (the bulletin only mentions single-channel printing uniformity with the other PRO films), so print_on is null.

FOURTH COLOUR LAYER: this film has a fourth colour-sensitive layer besides R, G and B. The spectral sensitivity plot draws it as a dashed curve labelled 'Cyan Sensitive Layer' (about 474-552 nm, peak about 0.42 on the y scale used here, i.e. below the blue/green/red curves). It is NOT traced; r, g and b are the three main layers.

curves: x is log H in lux-seconds as printed (daylight, 1/125 s), x axis runs -4.0 to 1.0, y axis 0 to 3.5; the three solid curves never touch and run from log H about -3.6 to about 0.67 (D-min plateaus about 0.95 b, 0.69 g, 0.17 r; the last point of a line can lie up to one 0.05 step beyond the drawn end). The labels Blue/Green/Red touch the curves but do not hide them.

sensitivity: the y axis has NO numbers, only a double arrow marking 1.0 between two horizontal rules. y is therefore set to 1.0 on the upper rule and 0.0 on the lower rule: the zero is arbitrary, only differences between points and between layers are meaningful (the curves reach down to about -0.75). Sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure in J/cm2 giving density 1.0 above D-min (Status M, C-41). The three solid curves cross each other and the dashed fourth-layer curve; blue starts at about 385 nm, green about 450 nm, red about 555 nm; they end in steep drops (blue about 516 nm, green about 595 nm, red about 665 nm), and since the tool keeps one y per x the last few nm of the steep edges are approximated.

dyes: not separate cyan/magenta/yellow dyes but two curves, Mid-scale Density (mid; typical densities for a mid-scale neutral subject) and Minimum Density (min; D-min), 400-720 nm, y = spectral diffuse density as printed (0-2.0+). Both start steep at 400 nm (mid about 1.97, min about 1.39). The drawn gridlines of this plot are not evenly spaced (0 / 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 are 36.5, 39.6 and 38.6 pt apart), so the y calibration is a least-squares fit and densities can be off by about 0.03.
Grain: diffuse RMS granularity value 4 (micro-densitometer aperture 48 um diameter, sample density 1.0 above minimum density; Fujifilm measurement, not comparable with colour reversal film).
